MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  April 7, 2025

Chair LeGaspi called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll call were
Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Brizuela, Commissioner Greenidge, Commissioner
Hoskins, Vice Chair Rosoff and Commissioner Apodaca. Also present was Rita Ruiz,
Public Safety Interim Director and Veronica Lomas, Management Analyst.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Hoskins motioned for the approval of the minutes of the Public Safety
Commission Meeting minutes that was held on March 3, 2025. Vice Chair Rosoff
seconded the motion.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins, Vice
  Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Greenidge
  and Commissioner Brizuela.
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Commissioner  Peña,  Commissioner  Fernandez-Silva  and
  Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

Mrs. Lomas advised that Rita Ruiz is now the Interim Director of Public Safety and Mr.
Newton will be overseeing the Office of Emergency Management. Rita states it is an
honor to be in this position and provided background of her previous work with the
Department of Justice and Homeland Security. Over the last 6 months, Mrs. Ruiz has had
the privilege of directly supporting Public Safety operations by coordinating street
takeover deployment strategies, managing public safety logistics for special events and
leading interdepartmental collaborations on key Public Safety initiatives. These efforts
have been aimed at increasing responsiveness, improving community safety and
ensuring a unified approach across departments.

Mrs. Lomas reports that National Telecommunications week is April 13th-April 19th, and
The Public Safety and Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department Dispatchers will be
recognized and will be receiving a proclamation at the next city council meeting on April
15, 2025. This week helps recognize the critical role and emergency response efforts that
are streamlined across the community. The dispatchers have received a total of 31,246
calls for service from January to year to date. The commissioners were given an update
and overview of the new Dispatch office and Room 1 will now be the Dispatch front
 counter to assist residents and the old Dispatch Office Room 15 will now be used for our
Public Affairs team.

Mrs. Lomas advised we will be providing a refresher on Blue Curb applications which will
be presented in upcoming meetings to the Commission. Mrs. Ruiz proceeds with going
over the application, which requires the applicant to obtain signatures from 9 surrounding
neighbors. Once the application has been completed and submitted by the applicant, it
will be presented to the Commission with photos of the property and where the blue curb
would be placed. The Commission will then approve or deny the request, once it is
approved it will go to the Council for consent and approval. The last step would be working
with Engineering to get the curb painted with proper signage once it is approved.

Mrs. Lomas reported that the Cadet Program will be moving to the Community Safety
Partnership Team from the Office of Emergency Management. Mrs. Ruiz provides insight
on our Cadet Advisor, Betsy Carranza who is working directly under Sgt. Munoz from the
Quadrant Team. This move will help build the connection between the community,
businesses and provide more opportunity for fundraising in the program. Mrs. Ruiz added
that there will be Cadet promotions soon and that the program would like all Public Safety
Commissioners to attend. Information for that event will be provided soon.

STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Lomas went over the April 2025 calendar.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

Chair Legaspi asked if applicants for Blue Curb are aware that anyone with a Handicap
Placard can park in that spot if the curb is painted blue. Mrs. Ruiz advised that we do
make applicants aware and educate them as the parking spot is on city property and is
open to the public with a valid Handicap Placard. Vice Chair Rosoff questioned if we have
that information printed on the Blue Curb application. Mrs. Ruiz advised that it is in the
municipal code, on the application and the applicant will be reminded when their
application is submitted to Mrs. Lomas.

Vice Chair Rosoff commented that the street takeovers at 5 points have started up again
and have occurred in the early mornings. Vice Chair Rosoff provides suggestions for
placing the decoy or camera trailers out.

Commissioner Brizeula advised that the crosswalk on Crossdale Ave. and Rosecrans
Ave. is a safety hazard for pedestrians as vehicles are not stopping and do not pay
attention to the flashing lights that make them aware that a pedestrian is crossing. Mrs.
Ruiz makes note of the location and concern.
Commissioner Hoskin advised of a concern on Dalwood Ave. and Alondra Blvd. regarding
vehicles parking in the area without Preferential Permits as they wait to pick up students
 from the college and are littering in the area while they wait in their vehicles.
Commissioner Hoskins also advised of the increase in transient activity in that area and
along Alondra Blvd. Mrs. Ruiz makes note of the concern to share with the team.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 6:27 PM.

_______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
